behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._get_specific_rendering_values -> outbound POST https://api.iyzipay.com/payment/iyzipos/checkoutform/initialize/auth/ecom (CF-initialize; sandbox-api.iyzipay.com in test) then redirect to the hosted paymentPageUrl
behavioral_notes.observation: Iyzico is a hosted-redirect acquirer but, unlike ECPay, it FIRST makes a server-to-server CF-initialize call. For code=='iyzico', _get_specific_rendering_values builds the payload via _iyzico_prepare_cf_initialize_payload (basketItems with a dummy 'Odoo purchase' VIRTUAL item, billingAddress + buyer blocks from the partner -- name split by payment_utils.split_partner_name, identityNumber=str(partner_id).zfill(5), ip='0' -- callbackUrl=urljoin(base_url, const.PAYMENT_RETURN_ROUTE)+'?tx_ref=<reference>', conversationId=self.reference, currency=currency_id.name, locale='tr' if env.lang=='tr_TR' else 'en', paidPrice/price=self.amount, paymentSource='ODOO') and POSTs it through the parent engine via self._send_api_request('POST', 'payment/iyzipos/checkoutform/initialize/auth/ecom', json=payload). On ValidationError it _set_error(...) and returns {}. The response's paymentPageUrl is parsed (werkzeug url_parse/url_decode) into api_url + url_params and handed to the QWeb redirect_form, so the browser is redirected (GET) to Iyzico's hosted Checkout Form. The outbound endpoint, the CF payload, and the hosted-redirect handoff are invisible to Python field/model metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.provider._build_request_headers / _iyzico_calculate_signature -> IYZWSv2 HMAC-SHA256 Authorization header (NOT a per-message webhook signature); _build_request_url selects api.iyzipay.com vs sandbox-api.iyzipay.com
behavioral_notes.observation: Outbound auth is Iyzico's IYZWSv2 HMAC-SHA256 scheme, configured on payment.provider (the module imports base64/hmac/hashlib/json/random/string). _build_request_url returns https://api.iyzipay.com when state=='enabled' else https://sandbox-api.iyzipay.com, joined with the endpoint. _build_request_headers generates an 8-char random_string (random.SystemRandom over ascii_letters+digits), computes signature=_iyzico_calculate_signature(endpoint, payload, random_string), assembles authorization_params=['apiKey:<iyzico_key_id>','randomKey:<random_string>','signature:<signature>'], base64-encodes '&'.join(...) and returns {'Authorization': f'IYZWSv2 {hash_base64}', 'x-iyzi-rnd': random_string}. _iyzico_calculate_signature builds data_string = f'{random_string}/{endpoint}{json.dumps(payload)}' and returns hmac.new(iyzico_key_secret, data_string, sha256).hexdigest(). _parse_response_content rejects (ValidationError 'The payment provider rejected the request.') unless response.json()['status']=='success'; _parse_response_error reads response.json()['errorMessage']. The actual HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request (requests.request) in the parent engine. The IYZWSv2 header construction, the HMAC over '{rnd}/{endpoint}{payload}', the sandbox/prod hosts, and the status=='success' gate are all invisible to metadata. NB: this signature authenticates Odoo's OUTBOUND requests; it is NOT used to verify inbound webhooks (see the controller note).

behavioral_notes.element: IyzicoController.iyzico_webhook (/payment/iyzico/webhook) & iyzico_return_from_payment (/payment/iyzico/return) -> NO local signature; authenticity by RE-FETCH via POST .../checkoutform/auth/ecom/detail; _apply_updates maps paymentStatus to pending/done/error
behavioral_notes.observation: Iyzico does NOT verify a per-message signature on its callbacks. Both public, csrf=False routes extract a one-time 'token' and delegate to the staticmethod _verify_and_process(tx_ref, token): the return route (POST, save_session=False) reads tx_ref from the query string + 'token' from the form; the webhook (POST) reads request.get_json_data() and uses data['paymentConversationId'] as the tx_ref and data['token']. _verify_and_process locates the tx with payment.transaction._search_by_reference('iyzico', {'reference': tx_ref}) -- note Iyzico does NOT override _extract_reference, so the base hook reads payment_data['reference'], i.e. the tx_ref passed in -- and, if found, performs a SECOND server-to-server call tx_sudo._send_api_request('POST', 'payment/iyzipos/checkoutform/auth/ecom/detail', json={conversationId, locale, token}) to RETRIEVE the authoritative payment detail straight from Iyzico (the IYZWSv2-signed CF-detail/retrieve endpoint), then tx_sudo._process('iyzico', verified_payment_data). Authenticity therefore comes from re-fetching the result over the authenticated API using the opaque token -- the callback body itself is never trusted -- and a failed re-fetch (ValidationError) is logged and dropped. _apply_updates writes provider_reference=data['paymentId'], picks the brand payment.method (cardAssociation via const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING {amex->american_express, mastercard->master_card} when cardType set; payment.payment_method_bank_transfer when bankName set; else payment.payment_method_unknown), then maps const.PAYMENT_STATUS_MAPPING on data['paymentStatus']: INIT_THREEDS/CALLBACK_THREEDS/INIT_BANK_TRANSFER/INIT_CREDIT/PENDING_CREDIT -> _set_pending; SUCCESS -> _set_done; FAILURE -> _set_error(errorMessage); anything else -> _set_error('Unknown status code'). The re-fetch-for-authenticity pattern and the three-way state mapping are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, IYZWSv2 keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; endpoints https://api.iyzipay.com (production) and https://sandbox-api.iyzipay.com (sandbox), selected by _build_request_url in models/payment_provider.py. Concrete endpoints reached (both via the parent payment.provider._send_api_request, requests.request): payment/iyzipos/checkoutform/initialize/auth/ecom (CF-initialize, outbound at checkout) and payment/iyzipos/checkoutform/auth/ecom/detail (CF-detail/retrieve, called from the controller to re-fetch and verify the result). Auth is the IYZWSv2 HMAC-SHA256 header (apiKey=iyzico_key_id public, signing secret=iyzico_key_secret base.group_system) plus x-iyzi-rnd. No 'requests' import here and no python iyzipay SDK: HTTP is delegated to the parent engine, which payment_iyzico configures via _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_content / _parse_response_error overrides. There is NO client-side SDK -- the browser is only redirected to Iyzico's hosted Checkout Form. This server-to-server REST link (with the re-fetch-as-verification idiom) is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of the endpoints, the IYZWSv2 auth, or the inbound trust model is reachable from model/field metadata.

external_integrations.auth: IYZWSv2 HMAC-SHA256 Authorization header -- apiKey=iyzico_key_id (public), HMAC-SHA256 of '{randomKey}/{endpoint}{json payload}' keyed by iyzico_key_secret (base.group_system), base64-wrapped, plus x-iyzi-rnd (_build_request_headers / _iyzico_calculate_signature)
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.iyzipay.com (CF-initialize for the hosted-redirect flow) authenticated with the IYZWSv2 HMAC-SHA256 scheme; a browser redirect to Iyzico's hosted Checkout Form (no client SDK); and inbound settlement via a webhook + return that DO NOT verify a per-message signature but instead re-fetch the authoritative result through the authenticated CF-detail endpoint using the one-time token. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is the Iyzico (Turkey) override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Iyzico endpoints, the IYZWSv2 HMAC auth, or -- most notably -- the re-fetch-as-verification trust model (no local signature on callbacks) are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py + const.py.

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_iyzico is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the payer (cardholder) and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Iyzico's Turkish-market card network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (IYZWSv2 API Key + Secret Key management, payment-method and currency enablement), service provisioning (initializing the Iyzico Checkout Form per transaction and confirming it by re-fetching CF-detail), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.iyzipay.com link, the hosted-redirect Checkout Form, and the token-re-fetch webhook/return settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Iyzico realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_xendit / payment_stripe records (network/support) and the parent payment engine; Iyzico is distinctive in verifying callbacks by re-fetching the authoritative result rather than by checking a local signature.
